title: Clarification Timing Does Not Mitigate Anchoring Bias in Tool-Using LLM Agents

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The purpose of the contribution is to test whether forcing clarification before retrieval exposure mitigates anchoring bias in tool-using LLM agents. Paper [2] explicitly studies anchoring bias in large language models, but it does not test mitigation strategies like forcing clarification before retrieval exposure. Paper [4] addresses bias mitigation in LLM-based agents but focuses on optimizing source selection for fair and balanced knowledge retrieval, which is not equivalent to the specific purpose of mitigating anchoring bias via clarification. Paper [9] studies anchoring bias in information retrieval settings but does not address mitigation strategies or tool-using LLM agents. No prior paper establishes the same purpose of testing clarification as a mitigation strategy for anchoring bias in tool-using LLM agents.

### Mechanism
The mechanism involves a controlled three-condition experiment (search-first baseline, IRG clarify-first, candidate-order control) on a specific dataset (InteractComp-Anchor) with a pre-registered evaluation setup. Paper [9] studies anchoring bias in information retrieval settings and provides evidence of anchoring during relevance estimation, but it does not use a controlled three-condition experiment or the specific mechanism of forcing clarification before retrieval exposure. Paper [12] introduces a framework (CLAM) for prompting language models to ask clarifying questions for ambiguous user queries, which is conceptually similar to the clarify-first condition in the contribution. However, CLAM focuses on ambiguous questions rather than anchoring bias mitigation, and it does not involve a three-condition experimental design. No prior paper uses the same mechanism as the contribution.

### Evaluation
The evaluation design involves a controlled three-condition experiment with a pre-registered success criterion, measuring the effect of the Intent Reconstruction Gate (IRG) on anchoring bias. Paper [9] uses a similar evaluation design to study anchoring bias in information retrieval, including controlled experiments and statistical analysis of user behavior. While the specific dataset and experimental setup differ, the evaluation design is substantively equivalent, as it involves controlled experiments to measure the impact of anchoring bias. Therefore, the evaluation facet is covered.

### Domain
The domain is anchoring bias in tool-using LLM agents. Paper [2] explicitly studies anchoring bias in large language models, which is the same general application area. Paper [9] studies anchoring bias in information retrieval, which is conceptually related but does not involve tool-using LLM agents. However, the domain of anchoring bias in tool-using LLM agents is not directly addressed in any prior paper. Therefore, the domain facet is not covered.
